sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the shapes
sections.what: Loads the validation tools and the standard type names used by the shapes below.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Removing an import that a shape uses will stop the file from loading.

sections.name: ModelCreate
sections.title: Shape for creating a model
sections.what: Describes a new model: name, start year and horizon years are required. Currency, unit divisor and granularity have defaults.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the common fields optional while keeping the core ones required.
sections.watch_out: Changing a default silently changes what every new model receives.

sections.name: ModelResponse
sections.title: Shape for a model reply
sections.what: Describes a model returned to the caller, including its id and timestamps. It can be built straight from a database record.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the route return the database record without copying fields by hand.
sections.watch_out: Every field here must exist on the database model, or replies will fail.

sections.name: ScenarioCreate
sections.title: Shape for creating a scenario
sections.what: Describes a new scenario: model id and name are required, description is optional, and the default flag is false unless set.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here checks that the model id exists.

sections.name: ScenarioResponse
sections.title: Shape for a scenario reply
sections.what: Describes a scenario returned to the caller, built from a database record.
sections.why: Same reason as the model reply shape.
sections.watch_out: Same rule as the model reply: fields must match the database.

sections.name: CalculationRequest
sections.title: Shape for a calculation request
sections.what: Describes a calculation request that carries only a scenario id.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The request does not say which parts of the model to calculate.

sections.name: CalculationResponse
sections.title: Shape for a calculation reply
sections.what: Describes a calculation reply: scenario id, status, message and optional results.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Results are a loose dictionary, so their contents are not checked.

summary: Defines the shapes of data sent to and returned by the model, scenario and calculation routes, and checks them automatically.
purpose: Give every route a clear, checked format so bad input is rejected early.
why: Likely reason: keeps requests and replies consistent and lets the API describe itself.
how: Each class lists fields with their types and default values. The framework checks incoming data against them. Response classes can be built straight from database records.
inputs: Request data from callers and database records.
outputs: Checked data and the reply shapes sent back.
risks: Changing a field name or type changes what the API accepts and returns, which can break the frontend. Response fields must exist on the database records.
debug: If a request fails validation, compare its field names and types with the matching class. If a reply is missing data, check that the database record has that field.
